description: The Tamanrasset geomagnetic observatory (IAGA code TAM) in southern Algeria was created in 1935 by the Institut de physique du globe d'Alger, modernised in 1992, and is run by the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris with CRAAG. It sits at 1,373 metres, at co-latitude 67.208 degrees and longitude 5.530 degrees, and records in HDZF orientation with a DI-flux theodolite, proton and Overhauser scalar magnetometers and an IPGP fluxgate vector magnetometer. The BCMT page gives the data available: a real-time display at one-minute resolution, one-second data and derived means, quasi-definitive data with about two months' latency and definitive data with about one year's latency, served through the BCMT data download, plot and real-time pages alongside geomagnetic indices and yearbooks. Access is free online under the BCMT terms of use. Caveats: the page is a station sheet, and download formats and licence details are on other BCMT pages. Coverage is the Tamanrasset site, one of the observatories in the BCMT network listed on the page. It supports hazard exposure analysis of geomagnetic storms for power grids and pipelines, and calibration of space weather models at low latitudes; related records are INTERMAGNET and the Kiruna magnetometer data.
